page1.text:
How did this happen?
I tucked myself in, closed my eyes, and said goodnight. But the next thing I knew, everything was red.

page3.text:
Mom woke me up before the noise did.
It was so bright, even though it was still nighttime.
Dad picked me up, then ran down the burning hallway.

page5.text:
I heard Mom's voice behind me.
She told Dad not to go on his own.
He ruffled my hair and told me to wait outside.
I nodded and did what he said.

page7.text:
Outside was the same as inside.
Everyone was all red, and my eyes hurt.
So I closed my eyes and ran, trying to find somewhere that wasn't so hot.
When I turned back to look, my house was already gone.
It must be punishment for not following directions.

page9.text:
I cry while I walk.
I know I have to go home and wait,
but I don't know where home is anymore.
I stop covering my face with my hand and look up.

page10.text: I come face to face with it all for the first time.

page11.text:
The town is burning in the distance.
The fire won't go out. It's too late to change it now.
This all happened ten years ago.
The flames burning far away are so distant, not physically, but in time.

page12.text:
"So...hot..."
My skin hurts.
My throat burns with every breath.
My body creaks with each movement of life.
When I try to run away, my ankles twist, caught on something heavy like shackles.
Even as a child, I somehow intuit that the death of everyone around me is dragging my living self down with them.

page13.text:
"Huh...?"
...It's still hot.
I claw at my throat, my nails scratching it red.
Each breath I suck in inflicts stabbing pain on my burned esophagus.
My eyeballs stop working, and my brain begins to steam in my skull.

page14.text:
"Why..."
It's hot.
It's hot, so hot. Hot, hot, hot. Hot, hot, hot, hot, hot, hot, hot, hothothothothothothot...!!!

page15.text:
"Ha...ah..."
I remember.
This is hot. Awfully hot.
But it's cold. Terribly cold.

page16.text:
Past the boiling point and back to freezing temperature.
My burning blood has already hardened and stopped. Everything I see is backwards.
And it's hot.
So it's cold.
That's why it's so hot I'm losing my mind.

page17.text:
However...
What was the cause of it all?

page18.text:
...
There was a black sun in the sky.
Didn't feel especially strange to me that the sun was out at night, or that it was black.
After all, everything was crazy.
It felt normal next to everything that was going on.

page19.text:
"Ah...ah...!"
And yet, I ran away.
I was so scared.
The fire around me wasn't scary.
Compared to that black shadow, getting burned to death felt only human, only natural.
So I ran.
I knew that if it caught me, it would take me someplace even scarier.

page20.text:
I look up at the sky in a daze.
I know it'll rain eventually, and I slowly lower my upraised hand...

page21.text:
"...Ah."
Slowly, I open my eyelids.
Not quite fully awake, I stare at my bedroom in a daze.

page22.text:
"A dream, huh?"
Still lying on my back, I feel relief.
How many years has it been since I woke up from a dream feeling relieved?

page23.text:
"But...it was such a clear dream."
I murmur aloud, still feeling the heat on my cheeks.
A long time ago, this nightmare used to haunt me and make me cry out at night.

page24.text:
...It happened ten years ago.
The memories were still fresh back then. Every time I went to sleep, I would find myself wandering in that inferno.
I never imagined that I'd forget about it, especially while I was in the dream.
When I fell asleep, it would all become real again—the sky that day, the burnt odor in the air, and the inescapable wall of fire.

page25.text:
...
Even now, I think that hasn't changed.
But it isn't as raw anymore.
With time, wounds heal and memories dull.
Over the last few years, all I really see when I dream about the fire is the color red.
Why would it come back again in vivid detail, even down to the smell of ash in the air, after all this time...?

page26.text:
...
And what was that?
I don't know what that thing was, nor do I remember it.
In fact, I didn't even see it.

page27.text:
"Argh..."
I want to throw up.
Just thinking about it makes me dizzy.
A circuit breaker flips in my body and tells me not to think about it any further.

page28.text:
"I should get up. Wash my face."
I'm drenched in sweat because of the nightmare.
I don't want my sheets to soak it up and get all gross, plus my brain is in a fog.

page29.text:
"Wait...what...?"
My arms feel sluggish.
In fact, I can't put any strength into them, and I can't even get up.

page30.text:
"Wait—what the hell?"
Damn it, even talking is a challenge.
I slowly bring my hand to my face, and realize it's pretty warm.

page31.text:
"...Wow. Did I catch a cold, too?"
That's a surprise.
This is the first time I've ever caught a cold.
I've lost count of the number of times I've been battered and bruised, but I've never gotten a common cold before.

page32.text: "...Maybe that's why I had the dream. I'm burning up, so I was burning in my dreams, too."

page33.text:
Yeah, that makes sense.
I can't think straight, so it's little wonder I'd have a dream or two—
"Ah..."
Whoa, WHOA WHOA WHOA WHOA WAIT what am I lying around for!?

page34.text:
"Uh, wait, why, how!?"
I frantically sit up.
Then, I check under the covers.
This is hardly the time to be worrying about feeling sluggish or tired.

page35.text:
If anything happened, then I need to run to the bathroom in the morning and destroy the evidence. My first priority is to purify myself and then exercise my right to silence.
To be frank, Shirou's stock in the Emiya household is in free fall.

page36.text:
"...Oh, it wasn't that bad."
Thank god.
My entire body is drenched in sweat, but there isn't really anything else off about it.

page37.text:
"That was a...dream, right? Yeah. It was that kind of dream."
There's no way I went to school while I was asleep, and I've never done anything that crazy with Tohsaka.
My subconscious went there all on its own.
After all, I'm still in the clothes I was wearing when I went to bed, and Saber's been in the room next door the entire time!

page38.text:
"...Yeah, Saber would've noticed if I went outside."
I sigh in palpable relief.
At once, the tension drains from my body, and I dramatically fall back on the floor.

page39.text:
"Shirou...? I just heard a noise. Is something wrong?"
I hear Saber's voice behind the sliding door.
...See?
Even that was enough to get her attention, so it had to be a dream. Yup, a dream. It was absolutely, positively a dream. If it wasn't, then I don't know how I'll look Tohsaka in the eye ever again.

page41.text:
"What is the matter? It's not like you to greet someone while lying down."
"Oh, I just woke up in a state I didn't expect."

page42.text:
Saber looks puzzled.
Now...
I'm thanking my lucky stars that was only a dream, but now I have to confront a different trial.
I feel slow and I can't even stand up, so how am I supposed to make breakfast...?

page43.text:
"37.6 degrees. Hmm. It's pretty unusual for you to catch a cold, Shirou."
She casually gives me my diagnosis, thermometer in one hand.
I already figured that was the case so it doesn't come as a surprise, but a cold would make me feel this heavy, huh?

page44.text:
"Does it hurt anywhere else? Like your throat or your head?"
"? No, not really. My body just feels all heavy and hot. Is that weird?"

page45.text:
"Mmm...I think that's a better sign than actual pain.
Oh, but you're a tough kid, so maybe you don't even notice the discomfort. ...Okay, I'll get you some medicine just in case."

page46.text:
Fuji-nee takes some cold medication and cough drops out of the first aid box.
She's an old hand at patching up lacerations and the like, but it looks like she isn't used to treating illnesses like this.

page47.text:
"Thanks, Fuji-nee. And sorry—I don't think I can make breakfast."
"Don't be stupid. Which do you think is more important, breakfast or your health? I'm glad Saber called me over, but if you'd gone ahead and cooked as usual, I would have been really pissed off!"

page48.text:
She growls in sincere anger.
...She's right, obviously.

page49.text:
"And don't worry about food. Sakura made okayu—rice porridge—so eat that if you get hungry."
"Huh? Sakura made porridge?"
She must be feeling better, then.

page50.text:
"Sakura, are you doing okay? You seemed in even worse shape than me yesterday."
"Yes. My fever is down, so you don't need to worry about me.
I managed to sleep well. It's all thanks to you keeping me company, so I wasn't scared."

page51.text:
...Oh, that's good.
I thought it would take longer, but I'm relieved that it took her only a night to recover.

page52.text:
"Oh yeah, I totally forgot. Sakura caught a cold yesterday, too."
"Huh...? Yeah, so? ...I don't like that look on your face, so stop whatever you're about to say."

page53.text:
"Mm-hmm. Shirou, did you try to transfer Sakura's cold over?"
"Uh, what? Why would I do that?"
"Oh, you don't get it? Sakura's fever is down, right? So maybe you did something. It's long been said that people get better from a cold when they pass it to someone else."

page54.text:
"...?"
I look at Sakura, not understanding.
"Oh..."
Finally, I realize what Fuji-nee's running her mouth off about.

page55.text:
"Y-y-y-you idiot! I only went over to take her temperature and give her medicine! You're not allowed to make any more of those jokes! It's rude to Sakura!"
I feel myself blushing furiously.
I imagine my 37-degree fever just climbed to 38.

page56.text:
"Just kidding! I know that, silly! You aren't clever enough for that."
"Urgh... That kinda annoys me too, but it's fine as long as that's cleared up."

page57.text:
"Good boy. I'll have the school excuse your absence, so take it easy today. Saber, would you mind taking care of Shirou?
There's no telling what he'll get up to, so tie him up in bed if you have to."

page58.text:
"I already intend to do so. I will keep a watchful eye on Shirou to make sure he does not get up. Should I also feed him?"
"Wow, that's a little intense, but it works for me. Thanks, Saber."

page59.text:
Saber nods.
...Is it just me, or did I just get a vague feeling of danger?

page60.text: "So, you listen to whatever Saber says, and behave until we come home. I'll buy something for dinner that'll give you energy, so you need to let yourself rest and recover."

page61.text:
Fuji-nee nods with a smile at the impossible mission she's giving me.
"...?"
Behind her, Sakura looks downcast. She looks like she wants to say something that's weighing on her mind.

page62.text:
"We're leaving! Look forward to the souvenirs!"
Fuji-nee waves goodbye and leaves for work.

page63.text:
"...Whew."
I see Fuji-nee off, then go back to bed.
All I did was go from my bedroom to a porch, but the effort made me so short of breath I collapsed right back into bed.
...My fever isn't that high, but evidently, I'm physically exhausted.
Fuji-nee's right. I won't be able to do much until I recover my strength in bed.

page64.text:
Then...
Sakura comes to my room, even though it's already past 7:30.

page65.text: "Sakura? It's already 7:30. Shouldn't you leave before you're late for school?"

page66.text:
"..."
Sakura awkwardly avoids meeting my gaze.
Just as I notice that she's making the same expression as earlier when she looked like she wanted to say something,
"Um, Senpai. Can I stay here?"
She looks up and asks me a question.

page67.text:
"Hm?"
She means staying home from school, right?

page68.text:
"...Oh. Do you still have a fever?"
"No, my fever is down. I just..."
She hesitates, like it's hard to say.
Hm.
She does still look pale, and it isn't reasonable to expect her to fully recover overnight after how bad she looked yesterday.

page69.text:
"Right, you had a cold, too. But are you sure?
Don't you need to get your absence excused?"
"...I'm sure. Um, I was thinking about playing hooky."
"Hm?"
She means skipping class by pretending to be sick?

page70.text: "Why? You actually have a cold, so it isn't lying. If you have a fever, you should sleep in your room."

page71.text:
"...Um. I'm saying that I feel fine."
"???"
I understand even less now.
What's Sakura trying to say?

page72.text:
"W-well, I think it's my fault that you caught a cold."
"Hey, don't just take what Fuji-nee says at face value. That's not what happened. I've been going out for late-night walks lately, so it's my own fault."

page73.text: "But still! ...I feel fine, so I'm going to play hooky t-to thank you for yesterday!"

page74.text:
"Mrgh."
Apparently, Sakura feels responsible for my illness.

page75.text:
If I'm being honest, I would feel better having her around.
Saber needs to sleep, and it would be easier for me if Sakura could prepare the medicine.

page76.text:
"Um, Senpai...?"
"Okay. Then I'm counting on you, Sakura."
"Of course, I know you have Saber, so you don't need—
Wait, what?"
"I'm asking you to take care of me."

page77.text:
"Um... you mean me, right?"
"Yeah. Saber's still jet-lagged, so she sleeps during the day. I know it's pathetic of me to ask, but I'd appreciate it if you could make lunch today."
"O-okay!
I'll do my best, Senpai!"
